proposals.title: Write ADR-002 and implement positional RNG rand() in packages/core
proposals.why_now: rand(masterSeed, namespace, ...coordinates) is the sole entropy source for every world value: all price layers, all macro events, all bot decisions, all NPC tip truth values. ADR-002 marks the hash function as DEFINIR with a specific start-point recommendation (SplitMix64 over FNV-1a) and requires bit-by-bit specification in an ADR before any implementation. Without rand(), packages/world cannot begin, INV-02 (direct tick query equals sequential advance) and INV-03 (player actions do not alter worldPrice) cannot be verified, and the price generator — an explicit FASE-1 deliverable — is unblocked only after this ADR is written and accepted. Nominal types are now in core so the only remaining prerequisite is the ADR itself.

proposals.title: Write ADR-004 and implement bigint division helpers with explicit rounding modes in packages/core
proposals.why_now: ADR-003 prohibits the / operator on economic types. ADR-004 mandates that every division declares one of three modes (TRUNCATE_TOWARD_ZERO, ROUND_HALF_UP, ROUND_HALF_EVEN) and that calling division without a declared mode is a compile-time or lint error. The enforcement mechanism is a DEFINIR item requiring its own ADR before implementation. Without division helpers, packages/domain cannot compute fees, rounding residue, or any monetary split, and INV-07 (rounding residue fully accounts for all precision loss) cannot be verified. This work is fully independent of IDEA-001 and can proceed in parallel on a separate branch.

proposals.title: Implement multi-commodity double-entry ledger in packages/domain
proposals.why_now: The double-entry ledger is an explicit FASE-1 deliverable and is the sole state container through which every domain operation — spot buy, spot sell, fee booking, rounding residue posting, margin adjustment — must pass. Nominal types are now in core (TASK-0011). Once division helpers land (IDEA-002), there are no remaining DEFINIR items blocking the ledger. INV-04 (per-commodity zero-sum in every Transaction), INV-05 (BRL sum always zero), INV-06 (per-asset quantity sum always zero), and INV-07 (rounding residue accounted) are all ledger invariants required in the FASE-1 acceptance gate. Deferring the ledger defers the entire domain and application layers.

proposals.title: Electron minimum security scaffolding and installer for Windows and Linux (INV-29, FASE-1)
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires a minimum installer for Windows and Linux produced by CI — and the spec warns that discovering packaging, ABI, and cross-platform path problems at the end is unrecoverable. After 43 checkpoints, no Electron window has been produced and no installer has been built. This work is fully independent of all other FASE-1 tasks and can proceed on any branch without waiting for rand(), division helpers, or the ledger. Every additional cycle without an installer is a cycle in which ABI failures, electron-builder configuration errors, and native module rebuild issues remain hidden.

proposals.title: Implement world price generator (two assets, two noise layers) in packages/world
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires a price generator with at least two noise layers and two assets. It is the primary consumer of rand() and is the prerequisite for INV-02 (direct tick query equals sequential advance) and INV-03 (player actions do not alter worldPrice), both required in the CI gate. Two DEFINIR items must be resolved as part of this task: octave parameters must be placed in a versioned configuration file, and the fixed-point or lookup-table strategy for log-space price construction must be documented in an ADR since Math.sin, Math.exp, Math.log, and Math.pow are all prohibited in pure packages. This task has the highest risk of the five because the DEFINIR choices directly affect cross-platform determinism.

repository_assessment.current_state: Monorepo infrastructure is operational: TypeScript strict mode, ESLint determinism lint, package boundary checker, and CI test gate are all in place. packages/core exports CanonicalEncoder (ADR-009 written and accepted) and the five nominal branded types with scale constants (TASK-0011, most recent commit). All other packages — world, domain, application, narrative, contracts, adapters, ui — are empty stubs. tools/replay, tools/bench, tools/package are stubs. No Electron window exists; no installer has been produced. Only ADR-009 is on record; ADR-002 (hash function for positional RNG) and ADR-004 (division rounding enforcement) remain DEFINIR-open and unresolved.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: packages/core still lacks the positional RNG rand() and bigint division helpers — the two remaining foundational primitives in core. Without rand(), packages/world cannot begin and INV-02 and INV-03 cannot be verified. Without division helpers, packages/domain cannot perform any monetary arithmetic and INV-04 through INV-07 cannot be verified. Both are gated by DEFINIR items requiring their own ADRs before implementation.

warnings: Two DEFINIR decisions must each be resolved by a separate ADR before their respective implementations begin: (a) the hash function for positional RNG (ADR-002), which blocks packages/world; (b) the technical enforcement mechanism for rounding modes (ADR-004), which blocks packages/domain. These are independent ADRs and should be authored concurrently to avoid sequential delay on the critical path.

The world price generator (IDEA-005) requires a DEFINIR decision on the fixed-point or lookup-table strategy for log-space computation before any implementation can begin. Math.sin, Math.exp, Math.log, and Math.pow are all prohibited in pure packages by §13. The ADR must document the chosen strategy and prove cross-platform bit identity before any price code is written. This is a non-trivial numerical engineering problem and the highest-risk item in FASE-1.

FASE-1 acceptance explicitly states that a minimum installer for Windows and Linux must exist in FASE-1 'in minimum form, not at the end.' After 43 checkpoints, no installer has been produced. Every additional cycle without Electron packaging work risks discovering ABI, native module, and cross-platform path failures with no remaining time to correct architectural decisions.
